saints.name: St. Maria Goretti
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A poor Italian girl of eleven who died defending her purity and forgave her killer…
biography: Maria Teresa Goretti was born at Corinaldo, near Ancona, on 16 October 1890, the third of seven children of poor farm laborers. The family migrated to the Pontine Marshes, sharing a farmhouse at Le Ferriere with the Serenelli family; her father Luigi died of malaria when she was nine, and she kept house while her mother worked the fields.

On 5 July 1902, as she sat sewing on the doorstep, twenty-year-old Alessandro Serenelli seized her with an awl, intent on rape. She resisted, crying that it was a mortal sin; he stabbed her fourteen times, and she died in hospital at Nettuno the next day, aged eleven, forgiving him and wishing him in heaven with her.

Alessandro was condemned to thirty years in prison; converted at last by a dream in which Maria offered him lilies that burned in his hands, he was freed in 1929, begged her mother Assunta's forgiveness, and died a Capuchin lay brother in 1970.

Pope Pius XII canonized her on 24 June 1950 before some half a million faithful, her mother present — the first mother to witness her own child's canonization. She is the patroness of youth, of purity, and of victims of assault.
saints.knownFor: Her forgiveness of her killer and the defense of her purity.
